;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Southern Damascus offensive (April–May 2018)]]
***Syrian government forces declare [[Damascus]] and its surroundings "completely safe" for the first time since 2011, after taking [[Yarmouk Camp]] and [[Al-Hajar al-Aswad|Hajar al-Aswad]] from [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/syria-bashar-assad-retake-damascus-suburbs-isis-capital-completely-safe/ (CBS News)]
*[[Kha Maung Seik massacre]]
**[[Amnesty International]] releases a report claiming it has evidence that [[Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army|ARSA]] insurgents massacred nearly 100 Hindus in the village of Kha Maung Seik on August 25, 2017, the same day ARSA attacked security forces in [[Myanmar]]'s [[Rakhine State]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-44206372 (BBC News)]
*[[Israel]] announces it is the first country to use the new [[F-35 Lightning II]] fighter jet in combat operations. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-44210403 (BBC News)] [http://www.businessinsider.com/israels-f-35s-saw-combat-in-syrian-air-war-that-hit-russian-defenses-2018-5?r=UK&IR=T (''Business Insider'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*At least 16 people are killed and 38 wounded in [[Kandahar]], [[Afghanistan]], by the accidental detonation of a container of explosives while security forces were attempting to dispose of it. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/05/afghanistan-kandahar-city-hit-deadly-minibus-bomb-explosion-180522091836785.html (Al Jazeera)]

;International relations
*[[2018 North Korea–United States summit]], [[North Korea–United States relations]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] states there is a "very substantial chance" that the summit with [[North Korea]]n leader [[Kim Jong-un]] next month may not occur. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-44207986 (BBC News)]
*[[China–United States relations]], [[Economy of China]]
**The [[Ministry of Finance of the People's Republic of China|Chinese Finance Ministry]] announces it will cut import duties on passenger vehicles from 25% to 15% starting on July 1, just days after [[China]] and the [[United States|U.S.]] agreed to a ceasefire in their recent trade hostilities. [http://money.cnn.com/2018/05/22/news/economy/china-cuts-car-tariffs-imports/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Zimbabwe]] applies to rejoin the [[Commonwealth of Nations]]. Zimbabwe left the Commonwealth in 2003 following a [[Zimbabwean presidential election, 2002|disputed election]] the previous year and subsequent suspension from the organization. According to [[Commonwealth Secretary-General]] [[Patricia Scotland]], the application was made on May 15. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/05/zimbabwe-applies-rejoin-commonwealth-180522062016470.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[Environmental issues in India]]
**Police in [[Thoothukudi]], [[Tamil Nadu]], [[India]], [[Thoothukudi massacre|kill]] nine people who protested against [[Vedanta Resources]]' [[Sterlite Copper|copper smelter operation]], alleging that it is a major source of pollution and a risk to fisheries. [[Government of Tamil Nadu|State Minister]] [[D. Jayakumar]] says that it was "unavoidable" that the people were shot. [[Indian National Congress|National Congress]] opposition leader [[Rahul Gandhi]] calls the killings "state sponsored terrorism". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-vedanta-smelter-violence/at-least-nine-dead-after-police-fire-on-protesters-seeking-closure-of-indian-copper-smelter-idUSKCN1IN11X (Reuters)] [http://indianexpress.com/article/india/tuticorin-anti-sterlite-protests-live-updates-thoothukudi-5186473/lite/ (''Indian Express'')]
